dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Se o denominador de uma fração indica em quantas partes dividimos o inteiro, o que o número 12 na fração 4/12 nos diz sobre a segunda reta?
Tente dividir a segunda reta numérica em 12 partes iguais. Use o campo 'numline2_noLabel_denom' para definir esse número e veja como a reta se ajusta.
Agora que a reta está dividida em 12 partes, conte 4 desses pequenos espaços a partir do zero para marcar o ponto.
Ao marcar o ponto na quarta marcação de 12, ele fica exatamente alinhado com o ponto 1/3 da reta de cima? Se sim, eles representam a mesma distância!

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "Are they the same? Correct the equal sign."; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

dicas.texto: Look at the denominator to determine how many equal parts the whole must have.
Read the denominator of the fraction that will be represented on Line 2, then enter that number in the denominator field.
The denominator is the bottom number in the fraction shown for Line 2.
Enter the number of equal intervals required by the bottom number of 4/... and confirm the division.
The denominator tells how many equal intervals make up the whole line.
Take the bottom number of the target fraction and type it into the denominator field before confirming.
For 4/..., focus on the bottom number rather than the numerator.
Type the denominator of 4/... into the Line 2 field and press the confirmation control.
The numerator tells how many equal parts to count from zero.
Start at zero, count equal intervals using the numerator, and use the denominator to identify the size of each interval.
On Line 2, count four equal intervals from the zero endpoint.
Click the fourth division after zero on the twelve-part Line 2.
The numerator records the number of parts represented, while the denominator records the total parts.
Count the intervals from zero to the marked point on Line 2, then enter that count in the numerator field.
The marked point is four intervals from zero.
Type the number of selected intervals into R1_user; keep the displayed denominator unchanged.
Equivalent fractions name the same amount even when their numerators and denominators differ.
Compare the locations marked on Line 1 and Line 2 rather than comparing the digits separately.
Both marked points are at the same distance from zero.
Select the sign used when the two fractions represent the same quantity.
Before submitting, check that the two marked points match and that the comparison sign reflects their relationship.
Review the Line 2 partition, the marked point, the numerator field, and the comparison selector in order.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde marcas na reta com o número de intervalos (n-1)
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the number of marks rather than the number of intervals. The denominator counts the equal parts of the line.

nodes.description: Mark the point that represents 4/12 on Line 2.
nodes.instruction: Mark the point that represents 4/12 on Line 2.

hints.message: The numerator tells how many equal parts to count from zero.
Start at zero, count equal intervals using the numerator, and use the denominator to identify the size of each interval.
On Line 2, count four equal intervals from the zero endpoint.
Click the fourth division after zero on the twelve-part Line 2.

misconceptions.description: Aluno ignora a relação de equivalência e foca na diferença entre os numeradores
misconceptions.feedback: Different numerators do not by themselves show different positions. Compare the locations on the two number lines.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde a posição do numerador e denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You reversed the fraction. The numerator counts selected parts, while the denominator names the total number of equal parts.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator that completes the equivalent fraction on the right.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator that completes the equivalent fraction on the right.

hints.message: The numerator records the number of parts represented, while the denominator records the total parts.
Count the intervals from zero to the marked point on Line 2, then enter that count in the numerator field.
The marked point is four intervals from zero.
Type the number of selected intervals into R1_user; keep the displayed denominator unchanged.

nodes.description: Choose the comparison sign that shows whether the two marked points are the same.
nodes.instruction: Choose the comparison sign that shows whether the two marked points are the same.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions name the same amount even when their numerators and denominators differ.
Compare the locations marked on Line 1 and Line 2 rather than comparing the digits separately.
Both marked points are at the same distance from zero.
Select the sign used when the two fractions represent the same quantity.

misconceptions.description: Aluno ignora a relação de equivalência e foca na diferença entre os numeradores
misconceptions.feedback: You focused on the different numerators. Equivalent fractions can use different numbers while marking the same position.

nodes.description: Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction comparison.
nodes.instruction: Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction comparison.

hints.message: Before submitting, check that the two marked points match and that the comparison sign reflects their relationship.
Review the Line 2 partition, the marked point, the numerator field, and the comparison selector in order.
Make sure the right-hand fraction uses the twelve-part denominator and that the selected sign indicates equality.
When every component shows the completed equivalent-fraction comparison, press the Done button.
